title: NY State Assembly · District 49
area: Southern Brooklyn, including Bensonhurst, Dyker Heights, Sunset Park and Brooklyn's Chinatown along 8th Avenue.

context.text: Incumbent Lester Chang and Joyce Xiaoqiong Xie both advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot; the Democratic, Republican and Conservative Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled. Chang first won this seat in a November 2022 upset over longtime Assembly Member Peter Abbate Jr.

candidates.name: Lester Chang

summary.text: Lester Chang is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent seeking re-election. Born in New York City, he worked in banking, finance and global logistics and served in the U.S. Navy Reserve before winning the District 49 seat in 2022, defeating incumbent Peter Abbate Jr. Ballotpedia lists his committees as Aging, Banks, Cities, Education and Housing.

background.text: Born in New York City. According to his campaign website, he was born in public housing on the Lower East Side to Chinese immigrant parents, his father died when he was 8, and the family later settled in Brooklyn's Midwood neighborhood.
Graduated from Midwood High School, earned a B.S. in accounting from Brooklyn College (CUNY) and a master's degree in international transportation from SUNY Maritime College.

Began his career in banking and finance before moving into global logistics; his campaign website says he led operations across several Asian countries, and his official biography cites 20 years of management experience in global trade and logistics.

Served in the U.S. Navy Reserve for about 24 years, reaching the rank of Chief Warrant Officer (CWO3). His campaign website says he supported Homeland Security in Washington, D.C. and the U.S. Coast Guard at Fort Wadsworth after 9/11 and was deployed as a military analyst to Bagram Air Base, Afghanistan, in 2009 and 2010.

Is a member of the New York State Naval Militia and volunteered for state active duty from March 2020 to March 2021 in support of COVID-19 operations, including converting the Jacob Javits Convention Center into a field hospital.
Worked with the Board of Elections as a Poll Site Coordinator for more than 30 years, according to his official biography.

Won the November 8, 2022 general election for Assembly District 49, defeating incumbent Peter Abbate Jr.; he took office in 2023. His official biography describes the district as covering parts of Kings County.
Ballotpedia lists his current committee assignments as Aging, Banks, Cities, Education and Housing.
Volunteers on the executive committee of the local Chinatown American Legion Post 1291 and lives in Brooklyn.

priorities.text: Preserving merit-based admissions to specialized high schools and expanding charter-school availability.
Restricting how and where homeless shelters can be sited in residential neighborhoods.
Lowering costs for working families and small businesses, including studying longer-term (40- and 50-year) mortgages and expanding tax credits for child and dependent care.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he is a strong advocate for school choice and supports lifting the cap on the number of charter schools allowed in New York City.
positions.quote: He is strong advocate for school choice and believes in lifting the cap on charter schools in New York City.

record.text: Sponsored A6049, which would establish 'October 7th Remembrance Day' as a day of commemoration in New York State; the bill remains referred to the Ways and Means Committee.

Filed for a temporary restraining order to block a plan to house homeless individuals alongside long-term tenants at the Borough Park Apartments, after rallying with State Senator Steve Chan against the plan.
Called for a full investigation after reports that an asbestos inspection at the site of a proposed homeless shelter on 86th Street in Bensonhurst may never have been properly conducted.

candidates.researchNotes: The repo's July 2026 candidate-slate snapshot listed an additional 'Stop Mamdani Party' ballot line for Chang, and a Ballotpedia category tag also references that party for his page, but neither the district's general-election listing nor his opponent's page (both checked September 25, 2026) show that line for him, so it was not included here.

candidates.name: Joyce Xiaoqiong Xie

summary.text: Joyce Xiaoqiong Xie is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Lester Chang. In her Ballotpedia survey she describes herself as a State Committee member, former Community Education Council District 20 member, mother of three and longtime Brooklyn community advocate. Her stated platform covers cleaner and safer communities, immigrant rights, education, seniors and small businesses.

background.text: Describes herself as a State Committee member and a longtime Brooklyn community advocate.
Previously served as a member of Community Education Council District 20.
Describes herself as a devoted mother of three.
The Democratic primary for the seat on June 23, 2026 was canceled, and she is on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

priorities.text: Quality education for all, and support for seniors and small-business owners.

candidates.researchNotes: Xie has not previously held elected office, so she has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. Her background and priorities are drawn entirely from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no separate campaign website could be located, and none of her stated priorities maps to a clear stance on the fixed issue list without inferring beyond what she said.

researchNotes: Chang first won this seat in the November 2022 general election, unseating longtime incumbent Peter Abbate Jr. Vote data is drawn from the assembly-ny.json roll-call snapshot, which covers only May-June 2026 Assembly floor votes; most were near-unanimous procedural or public-employee-benefit bills, so the two contested votes shown here are the most notable available. Xie's biography rests on her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website or news profile was found, and her career and education are not documented there.
